subject: Transition to BYOK + Data Residency Addendum — next steps
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: acmecorp-legal@acme.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Residency addendum + BYOK questions

Rachel — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal asked me to confirm a couple of things before we loop procurement:

1) The BYOK flow: can Acme manage a customer-managed key (CMK) in our HSM/KMS and have Redwood never hold the unwrapped key material? We saw references to an "escrow" option in the docs — can you explain when that would be used?

2) Subprocessor disclosure: we need a current list of subprocessors that would touch metadata or telemetry for a private VPC deployment. If there are temporary contractors for support or on-call, please call that out.

3) Cross-border and export: Acme handles regulated EU-PHI and some EEA customers — what controls do you offer for preventing egress of model invocation logs outside the EU?

We’re aiming to close the DevOps procurement next week if the redlines are reasonable. Appreciate a short reply so I can share with legal.

—Lena
Product Privacy & Compliance
Acme Corp

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency addendum + BYOK questions

Thanks Lena — great to hear the timeline. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps.

1) BYOK / CMK: Yes. For Private (VPC or on-prem) deployments we support a BYOK model where Acme provisions the CMK in your KMS (cloud HSM or on-prem HSM) and Redwood never stores the plaintext key. Our runtime integrates with customer KMS via limited scopes (Encrypt/Decrypt for token envelopes) and uses per-request ephemeral wrapping keys. The "escrow" option is only considered when customers want a recoverable key in event of catastrophic key loss; that's opt-in and requires a notarized escrow arrangement and a separate escrow hold agreement.

2) Subprocessors: We will provide the full, current list in the next email (attached CSV). For Private deployments in your region we typically engage: our operator support team (Redwood staff located in NA/EU), cloud infrastructure partners for optional managed hosting, and a small set of vendor monitoring services (logs/metrics ingestion). Contractors are used infrequently; any contractor access is tiered and time-limited and appears in audit logs.

3) Cross-border/export: We can restrict telemetry and model invocation logs to EU regions in the private control plane, and we can disable certain nonessential telemetry by default. For EEA-PHI, we recommend: (a) VPC private control plane, (b) explicit egress rules at the account level, and (c) encryption-in-transit + envelope encryption via your CMK. We also offer contractual language restricting subprocessors from transferring data outside the EEA without consent.

Next steps I propose:
- I attach a draft Residency Addendum (v1) and a subprocessors snapshot. Please accept as a working draft.
- Irene, can you confirm whether the escrow language below is acceptable as a carve-out or needs additional guardrails?
- Grace, can you confirm the ops runbook/stateful telemetry we can flip off by default for Acme’s environment?

If this looks reasonable, we can generate a clean Docusign packet for legal review by Monday.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Director, Sales (Platform)
Redwood Inference

Irene / Grace — forwarding Acme’s legal questions (below). Key asks: escrow mechanics; explicit contractual prohibition on EEA egress of invocation logs; subprocessors detail.

Irene: the suggested escrow model in the attached addendum is intentionally high-level — it says: "Escrow is available only upon documented disaster recovery request and requires notarized custody & multi-party release controls." Legal may ask for more specifics around split control, K-of-N release, and on-site witness. Can you propose 2 short paragraph options: minimal (no escrow details beyond opt-in) and prescriptive (K-of-N + onshore escrow) we can share?

Grace: operations — can you confirm which telemetry flags we can set to OFF for Acme’s VPC private control plane (invocation logs, prompt prefetch cache traces, error-level traces) and whether we can guarantee those are region-bound? Also need a timeline for enabling BYOK for their staging environment (estimate: 3–5 business days once KMS policies are provisioned).

I left Acme on copy earlier — I’ll keep them in the loop but prefer legal Qs to be answered by you two so we don’t give blockers.

Thanks,
Rachel

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Residency addendum + BYOK questions — legal/op ops asks

Rachel / Grace — draft language below for two escrow options. I kept both concise so they could be inserted as DPA addendum clauses.

Option A (Minimal, customer-facing):
"Escrow: Customer may elect a key-escrow option for their CMK. Escrow is strictly opt-in and requires both parties to execute a separate Escrow Addendum that sets forth custody, access procedures, and a documented disaster recovery activation process. Escrow materials will be held by an agreed third-party custodian and will only be released upon jointly authenticated written request from authorized representatives."

Option B (Prescriptive, audit-friendly):
"Escrow: In cases where Customer elects escrow, key material will be split using K-of-N secret sharing and deposited with an industry-standard custodian located within the Customer’s jurisdiction. Release of key shares requires agreement from at least two authorized representatives from Redwood and two from the Customer and a notarized release request. Escrow access events will be logged, audited annually, and subject to a mutually agreed incident review process."

Regarding egress prohibition: we can provide a DPA clause that expressly prohibits export of invocation logs or PII-containing telemetry outside the EEA for EU-region deployments, except as required by law, with a 30-day notice and customer consent for any change. I recommend making the export-restriction clause a hard contractual SOW for Acme’s account.

I’ll polish the wording and I can drop those two paragraphs into the Residency Addendum and send a marked version for signature.

—Irene
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency addendum + BYOK questions

Lena — quick ops confirmation and timeline.

- Telemetry toggles: we can disable invocation logging, prompt prefetch traces, and error-level stack traces per environment. We will keep minimal service-level metrics (success/failure counts, latency histograms) for platform health; those metrics are aggregated and do not contain prompt text or PII.
- Regional binding: for Private VPC we will bind the control plane and telemetry collection endpoints to the customer’s chosen cloud region and block outbound egress via VPC firewall rules and routing. For on-prem we will run without any outbound telemetry by default unless you explicitly opt in.
- BYOK enablement: once Acme provides KMS IAM policy docs and a test key, we can enable BYOK in staging within 3 business days; production rollout typically follows a 7 business day validation window.

Attached: updated Residency_Addendum_v1 with Irene’s escrow Option B inserted and the subprocessors snapshot (timestamped). If this looks good to Acme legal, we’ll prepare a Docusign packet and a short Ops runbook for their security team.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
